description: This case study is the US Chemical Safety Board's investigation of the explosion at the BP America refinery in Texas City, Texas, at about 1:20 p.m. on 23 March 2005, with a final report approved by a 5-0 vote on 20 March 2007. During restart of a hydrocarbon isomerisation unit a distillation tower flooded and overpressurised, causing a geyser-like release from a vent stack and a series of explosions that killed 15 workers and injured 180, many in or around work trailers. The page links the final investigation report, a management of change report and a positive material verification safety bulletin, and lists recommendations with their closure status, for example to the American Petroleum Institute on siting occupied trailers and revising practices for relief systems. Access: free downloads from the CSB site; no licence is stated. Coverage is one refinery and the US refining industry standards. Caveats: only the investigation page was read, not the reports, and the total number of recommendations comes from search summaries. It suits emergency response and hazard exposure studies of refineries and process plant siting, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

outcomes: A series of explosions during the restart of a hydrocarbon isomerisation unit killed 15 workers and injured 180 others, most of the victims being in or near work trailers close to an atmospheric vent stack, after a distillation tower flooded with hydrocarbons and was overpressurised, causing a geyser-like release. The Board issued recommendations, including to the American Petroleum Institute on the siting of occupied trailers and on relief and disposal system practices, and search summaries count 26 recommendations to nine entities.
